checks.required_result: every References entry must be cited somewhere in the body; the profile admits only sources actually used, and an entry the body never touches is a lead or a deletion left behind
every source identifier the leaf prints must name a record the source library registers; an identifier that resolves to nothing reads exactly like one that resolves

the leaf's own research/source-bindings.toml must validate against the source library: every id one the library registers, every role and state a word the schema knows, and every reviewed state carrying the fingerprint the bound record computes to now. Authoring writes that file, so without this check nothing in the run holds it to the schema it is written against, and a fingerprint that has moved says the bound record moved: what rests on it is read again, never the new value pasted back

no artifact the leaf's research bound as restricted may have its bytes reproduced in the leaf, whether the leaf declares the reproduction by binding it as the translation control or prints it by attributing a set passage to it; the leaf's own self-consistency cannot see this, because the rights live in src/sources and nowhere in the document
every element key a component manifest relation joins must be claimed by the unit that carries that relation's evidence; the drift is invisible in either table alone
no source the References declare the guide does not quote may be credited with a printed quotation; the contradiction shows in neither statement alone

the leaf's \AIGenerationProvenance record must state this run: its workflow, version, source digest, run id and seed commit, as the packet header states them and not as the leaf's existing record or an earlier contribution's prose states them; the leaf cannot be held against the run by anything the leaf alone says, and a v10 copied out of prose survived a v11 pass because nothing held it

the leaf must carry the chronology corpus's own answer for its appointed loci in research/chronology.toml, and it must be the answer the corpus gives now; guidance/scripture-chronology.md section 14 requires a consumer to carry the stable ids -- event id, unit id, profile, relation -- so that prose can be regenerated without re-researching the fact, and a carried id that no longer names what the corpus holds is the second source of truth the corpus exists to prevent. The record is generated, so a leaf whose copy has drifted is rewritten from the corpus and never reconciled toward the guide

every biblical date the leaf prints must be an assertion the chronology corpus makes at the verses the element appoints, printed in the source's own label and carrying the corpus's subject and relation; and from this version the date cell of the scriptural dossier may hold no figure that is not inside such a claim, with one cell for every appointed Scripture including the ones the corpus dates nowhere. A well-formed year reads exactly like a right one, so a date recalled or researched into place is invisible to every other gate and to the leaf's own self-consistency
proper-components manifest must be valid
canonical PDF must build without fatal errors
synthesis PDF must build without fatal errors
the canonical PDF must exist for {proper}
the synthesis PDF must exist for {proper}
the proper-components manifest must be consistent with the built artifacts, and the brief synthesis must occupy exactly two pages
tracked revision timestamps and AI provenance must be valid in source and PDF

checks.command: awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} 'index($0, "- Authorized ") == 1 && index($0, "provider `" p "`, identity `" d "`.") > 0 { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' guidance/liturgy/propers-production-plan.md
checks.required_result: the production plan must still authorize exactly this provider and this identity at the moment of publication
the canonical PDF must be installed at pdf/{provider}/{proper}.pdf
the synthesis PDF must be installed at pdf/{provider}/{proper}-synthesis.pdf

checks.command: cmp -s build/{provider}/{proper}.pdf pdf/{provider}/{proper}.pdf && cmp -s build/{provider}/{proper}-synthesis.pdf pdf/{provider}/{proper}-synthesis.pdf
checks.required_result: each installed PDF must be byte-identical to the build artifact `final-acceptance` accepted; a file at the publication path proves only that something was installed, and the artifact the visual and mechanical gates passed is the one the reader must get
the component manifest must still be consistent with the built artifacts, and the brief synthesis must still occupy exactly two pages
tracked revision timestamps and AI provenance must be valid in the source and in the installed PDF, not only in the build tree
the leaf must carry a web-edition declaration; nothing defaults to eligible
the web-edition declaration must be valid for this leaf, and a leaf declared eligible must use no blocking construct
the canonical web edition must exist at web/{provider}/{proper}.md and be tracked, not merely generated into the build tree
the synthesis is a derived companion of the canonical leaf and has no web edition of its own; a separate -synthesis web leaf is a second prose authority
a per-publication release record must exist for the canonical publication
a per-publication release record must exist for the synthesis publication; the companion is published in its own right

checks.command: awk -v d={proper} 'function v(s) { sub(/^[ \t]*"[^"]*"[ \t]*:[ \t]*/, "", s); sub(/,[ \t]*$/, "", s); gsub(/^"|"$/, "", s); return s } { seen[FILENAME] = 1; if ($0 ~ /"schema_version"/) ver[FILENAME] = v($0); else if ($0 ~ /"id"/) id[FILENAME] = v($0); else if ($0 ~ /"catalog"/) cat[FILENAME] = v($0); else if ($0 ~ /"status"/) st[FILENAME] = v($0); else if ($0 ~ /"authorization"/) au[FILENAME] = v($0) } END { n = 0; for (f in seen) { n++; want = (f ~ /-synthesis\.json$/) ? d "-synthesis" : d; if (ver[f] != "1" || id[f] != want || cat[f] != "library/traditional-latin-mass.md" || st[f] != "alpha" || au[f] == "" || au[f] == "null") exit 1 } exit !(n == 2) }' release/publications/{provider}/{proper}.json release/publications/{provider}/{proper}-synthesis.json
checks.required_result: both release records must say what they are: schema version 1, an id naming this leaf and its synthesis companion, this catalog, status `alpha`, and a standing authorization rather than the null a held record carries. Existence proves a file was written; this proves it describes this publication

checks.command: awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} 'index($0, "](../pdf/" p "/" d ".pdf)")   > 0 { full = 1 } index($0, "](../pdf/" p "/" d "-synthesis.pdf)") > 0 { syn = 1 } index($0, "](../web/" p "/" d ".html)") > 0 { web = 1 } END { exit !(full && syn && web) }' library/traditional-latin-mass.md
checks.required_result: this provider's catalog cell must link all three published artifacts: the full PDF, the synthesis PDF, and the web edition

checks.command: awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} 'index($0, "](../pdf/" p "/" d ".pdf)") > 0 && index($0, "](../web/" p "/" d ".html)") > 0 { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' library/traditional-latin-mass.md && git ls-files --error-unmatch web/{provider}/{proper}.md >/dev/null 2>&1 && test ! -e web/{provider}/{proper}.html
checks.required_result: the catalog's `Read` link must name this provider's own web edition in the same row as this provider's PDF link, and the tracked Markdown the site renders that `.html` from must exist; the `.html` itself is generated at site build time from web/{provider}/{proper}.md and is never tracked, so a tracked `.html` beside it would be a second, hand-made page the build does not produce

checks.command: awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} -F'|' 'index($0, "](../pdf/" p "/" d ".pdf)") > 0 { rows++; mine = 0; if (NF < 5) bad = 1; for (i = 4; i < NF; i++) { cell = $i; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", cell); if (index(cell, "/" p "/") > 0) { mine++; continue } if (cell != "Planned" && index(cell, "](../") == 0) bad = 1 } if (mine != 1) bad = 1 } END { exit !(rows == 1 && !bad) }' library/traditional-latin-mass.md
checks.required_result: publishing one provider wires one cell: this identity must own exactly one catalog row, exactly one cell in it may name this provider's artifacts, and every other provider's cell in that row must still hold its own well-formed state -- the bare word `Planned` or links of its own. A gate runs mid-run and has no earlier commit to diff against, so the property is stated as one this provider's wiring cannot satisfy by overwriting a neighbour

checks.command: awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} 'FNR == NR { if (primary == "" && match($0, /"provider"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"[a-z0-9-]+"/)) { primary = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^.*: *"/, "", primary); sub(/"$/, "", primary) } next } { line = $0; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", line); if (line == "<!-- triptych-publication-id: " (p == primary ? d : p ":" d) " -->") found++ } END { exit !(primary != "" && found == 1) }' release/public-alpha.json library/traditional-latin-mass.md
checks.required_result: the catalog must carry this publication's stable marker in the form the release tooling reads: the bare leaf id for the manifest's primary provider and the `{provider}:` prefixed form for any other. The marker, not the link text, is what binds the row to the release record, so a wired cell without one is a publication the site cannot account for. Exactly one marker, too: a second copy is a wiring step that ran twice

every recorded site source must still hash to what is on disk, and this publication's tracked web edition must be one of them; `ADOPT=1` is what records a newly tracked edition, and an unrecorded source is a page the site authorization does not cover

the release policy must hold across every publication record, catalog occurrence and marker in the repository, and this publication's two records must be among the ones it just validated; the repository-wide schema and coverage rules are that tool's, and the gate asks it rather than restating them

checks.command: make check-document-catalogue && awk -v p={provider} -v d={proper} 'index($0, "\"pdf/" p "/" d ".pdf\"") > 0 { full = 1 } index($0, "\"pdf/" p "/" d "-synthesis.pdf\"") > 0 { syn = 1 } index($0, "\"web/" p "/" d ".html\"") > 0 { web = 1 } END { exit !(full && syn && web) }' src/web/data/structure/documents/corpus.json
checks.required_result: each document's title must still match the PDF it names and the tracked corpus catalogue must be what the sources produce now, and that catalogue must carry this publication's three artifacts: both PDFs and the rendered page the catalog's `Read` link points at. This is where the `.html` is proved to be a page the site derives, since the corpus is regenerated from the sources and checked against them
every tracked web edition must be exactly what current sources produce, this one included; the installed edition is the reviewed one only while the source it was converted from has not moved under it
